title: Secondary school teachers’ perspectives on GenAI proliferation: generating advanced insights
extended_summary:
This paper examines how the rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is affecting secondary education, with a particular focus on academic integrity, teaching practices, assessment, and teacher support needs. The central research question asks what significant challenges and opportunities Ontario secondary school teachers perceive as GenAI becomes more common in schools. The authors position the study as addressing a gap in the literature, noting that most prior discussion has centered on postsecondary education rather than secondary schools.

The study uses a qualitative interview design grounded in invitational education as a theoretical framework. Seventeen practising Ontario secondary school teachers from five publicly funded school boards were recruited and interviewed in semi-structured sessions lasting about 60 minutes. Data were collected between November 2023 and January 2024, transcribed, member-checked, and coded in Atlas.ti. The analysis produced three main themes: generating people, generating programs, and generating policies. These themes capture teachers’ calls for professional development and expertise-building, structured and transparent school programs for GenAI integration, and clear policies to govern acceptable use, academic integrity, and institutional expectations.

The population studied was high school teachers in southern Ontario, Canada, rather than students directly. Participants represented a range of teaching experience levels and subjects, but all were secondary educators working in public school boards. The study context is school-based secondary education, though the data come from interviews rather than classroom implementation of a specific AI tool or intervention.

The paper concludes that teachers see GenAI as both a disruptive challenge and a potentially valuable educational tool, but they feel underprepared and under-supported. The authors argue that effective GenAI integration requires coordinated action across three areas: teacher capacity-building through professional development, purposeful programs and practices for assessment and instruction, and adaptable policy frameworks that support ethical and equitable use. They emphasize collaboration among teachers, administrators, policymakers, parents, and other stakeholders, and propose a train-the-trainer style model using teacher champions to support scalable GenAI integration while preserving academic integrity.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative artificial intelligence tools broadly, including text-generating systems used in educational contexts; the paper discusses GenAI as a class rather than evaluating a single product.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied through Ontario secondary school teachers' perceptions of GenAI proliferation in relation to teaching, assessment, academic integrity, professional development, and policy needs. ChatGPT is mentioned only as an example, not as the evaluated product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative interview study of 17 Ontario secondary school teachers, not an experimental or quasi-experimental evaluation of an AI tool's effects on learner outcomes. The methodology is clear, but evidence is perception-based rather than causal.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived challenges and opportunities of GenAI integration but does not provide quantified effects on student learning or institutional outcomes. Impact is therefore unclear rather than demonstrated.
